newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy urges Albanians to stay at home.
newsitem.headline: Italy urges Albanians to stay at home.

text.p: Italy, faced with an exodus of fleeing Albanians, said on Sunday that Europe was committed to efforts to rebuild the Balkan state and urged would-be refugees to stay at home.

"The crisis will not be resolved by fleeing but by the rebuilding of Albania... Europe will provide the material conditions for this to happen," Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters on a visit to the southern port of Brindisi.
"This is an emergency situation and the objective is (to persuade Albanians) to stay in their homeland."
Antonio Ruggiero, the chief of police in Brindisi, indicated later that the Italian authorities would take a tougher line against ships bringing refugees to Italy.

The captain and crew of a fishing boat that arrived in Brindisi on Sunday evening with 142 Albanians on board were arrested for breaking the law on introducing illegal immigrants and for bringing firearms into the country.

"This decision should be seen as a strong signal to dissuade the traffic of Albanian citizens into Italy," said Ruggiero. "From now on all Albanian ships entering Brindisi with illegal immigrants on board will be placed under seizure."
The flood of refugees showed signs of subsiding on Sunday evening, with Italian coast guards saying that rough seas in the Adriatic had deterred the few boats remaining.

A ship with 253 Turkish citizens evacuated from the port of Durres docked in the port of Bari however. They were to be taken by bus to the city's airport where a Turkish airliner was scheduled to take them on to Turkey at midnight.

Prodi said that an EU mission scheduled to visit Tirana on Monday would seek to restore civil order. His remarks were later broadcast on Italian RAI state television with Albanian subtitles for the many viewers in that country.
Prodi's words were repeated later by Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano in a statement.
Thousands of terrified Albanian refugees have crossed the Adriatic in recent days in an array of old boats to escape the violence engulfing much of their impoverished country.
"We travelled with our hearts in our mouths," said 19-year-old student Kulluri Bardhxl after he was pulled off one overcrowded ship that ran aground on Saturday night.

The Foreign Ministry said Albania had asked for a meeting between Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and the European Union and said it could take place on March 24, when EU foreign ministers are due to meet in Brussels.

The EU, meeting in the Netherlands at the weekend, said it would send military and police advisers but ruled out military intervention to end the chaos that has swept Albania following the failure in January of fraudulent savings schemes.
Some 1,600 Albanians crossed in choppy conditions on Saturday night and Sunday morning, including 858 crammed onto a rusting navy ship who were rescued by coast guards.
Refugees were moved to hastily-organised "hospitality centres" set up in schools, offices and barracks and the mayor of Brindisi, Lorenzo Maggi, said his city was swamped.
"We were ready to accept a more modest-sized exodus. Today the phenomenon is taking on Biblical proportions," he said.
Hundreds of the Albanians, many carrying plastic bags of food, were later taken by bus to other cities further up the coast, relieving the pressure on the southern ports.
Some 760 were moved to accommodation in the central Italian towns of Pescara, Macerata, Ancona and Teramo.
